md_name: Single Amplified Genome Workflow for Extreme Archaeal Communities
md_description: This DAG represents the end-to-end data generation and processing workflow for single amplified genomes from archaeal communities collected in extreme environments such as hydrothermal vents. It covers sample collection under defined environmental conditions, cell lysis and amplification of genomic material, high-throughput sequencing, and downstream genome assembly and reconstruction. The resulting data support analysis of archaeal adaptation to extreme habitats and their roles in ecosystem biochemical processes.

archaeal_community_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic sample-identity and origin metadata for the archaeal community sample: where it was collected, what extreme environment it came from, and the in situ environmental parameters recorded at collection. I excluded lysis, amplification, sequencing, and computational fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating general experiment IDs since root-level identifiers should appear only once and none were provided as already_generated. The field set is kept minimal but sufficient to understand sample provenance and collection context.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the archaeal community sample at collection; string format example: 'SAG-EXT-0001'. Record once for each physical sample and use to link this sample to all downstream workflow steps.
Name of the environmental site where the sample was collected, such as a hydrothermal vent field, hot spring, or other extreme habitat; record at sampling time from field notes.
Broad category of the extreme environment from which the sample originated; record at collection to describe the habitat setting, not the experimental treatment.
Latitude of the sampling location in decimal degrees (range -90 to 90); record from GPS or site survey at the moment of collection.
Longitude of the sampling location in decimal degrees (range -180 to 180); record from GPS or site survey at the moment of collection.
Sampling depth in meters below surface or water level, depending on site context; record at collection if applicable for vents, water columns, or subsurface sites.

In situ temperature at the sample location in degrees Celsius; record at the time of collection using field instrumentation. Typical extreme-environment values may span from below 0 to above 100 Celsius depending on site.
In situ pH measured at the collection site; record at the time of sampling using field probe or validated site measurement. Typical range is 0 to 14.

In situ salinity or practical salinity units measured at collection; record at sampling when relevant for marine, hypersaline, or brine-associated habitats. Typical range is 0 to >300 PSU depending on site.
In situ redox potential in millivolts measured at collection; record at the sampling point when available to describe geochemical conditions of the archaeal habitat.
Physical matrix sampled from the environment; record at collection to describe what was actually collected, such as water, sediment, biofilm, or chimney material.

cell_lysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how cell lysis was performed: the lysis method, key reagent/buffer details, incubation conditions, mechanical disruption settings, and a post-step output quality indicator for lysis effectiveness. I excluded sample provenance fields because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded lysate properties as an output Entity. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I avoided only cross-node territory and kept the schema focused on reproducible process parameters.

md_schema.descr: Primary cell disruption approach used to lyse archaeal cells and release genomic material from the collected sample; record at the start of the process. Example values include chemical, enzymatic, mechanical, or combined lysis strategies.
Commercial or in-house lysis kit used for the process, if applicable; record the kit name exactly as used in the protocol, for example a bead-beating or archaeal DNA extraction kit.
Key reagents, buffers, or additives used during lysis, including concentrations when critical to the protocol; record at the bench during the lysis step.
Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the lysis reaction was incubated; record during the process. Typical values may range from 4 to 100 Celsius depending on chemistry or thermal treatment.
Duration of the lysis incubation in minutes; record the elapsed time the sample was held under lysis conditions.
Instrument used for mechanical lysis, if applicable, such as bead beater, homogenizer, or sonicator; record the device name/model used during the process.
Operational intensity setting for mechanical lysis, such as shaking speed, bead-beating frequency, or sonication power; record the instrument setting used during the process.
Qualitative indicator of whether the lysis step produced an adequate lysate for downstream amplification; record immediately after lysis based on operator assessment or protocol criteria.

lysate.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the post-lysis material itself, so I included intrinsic lysate properties that a downstream amplification step would need to know: what kind of lysate it is, its physical amount, and basic storage/handling state. I excluded lysis protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process, and I excluded amplification settings because those belong to the downstream Process. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I focused on non-overlapping lysate identity and condition attributes rather than repeating sample-origin metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the lysate derived from the archaeal community sample; string format example: 'LYS-0001'. Record once for this post-lysis material and use to link it to downstream amplification.
Identifier of the upstream archaeal community sample from which this lysate was produced; string format example: 'SAG-EXT-0001'. Use to trace lineage from the original sample to the lysate.
Observed physical state of the lysate after lysis and before amplification; record at transfer to the downstream process to indicate whether the material was clear, cloudy, particulate, or mixed.

Volume of lysate available for downstream amplification in microliters; measure or estimate at the point the lysate is aliquoted for the next step. Typical values may range from 1 to 1000 microliters.

Total DNA concentration in the lysate in nanograms per microliter, if measured before amplification; record at the handoff to downstream processing using the assay specified in the workflow. Typical values may be low and variable for single-cell or SAG inputs.
Storage temperature in degrees Celsius if the lysate was held prior to amplification; record at the time of storage or transfer. Typical values include 4, -20, or -80 Celsius.
Time in hours between lysate preparation and downstream amplification, or total storage duration if held before use; record at the point of transfer to amplification.
Whether the lysate underwent any cleanup or clarification before amplification; record at the handoff to indicate if debris removal or purification was performed.

isothermal_amplification.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only amplification protocol parameters and process-quality indicators: kit identity, enzyme mix, temperature/time profile, reaction volume, cycle count, and a simple success flag. I excluded lysate properties because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded amplified library attributes because those are output Entity fields. No already_generated fields were provided for this step, so I avoided overlap by keeping the schema strictly about how the amplification was run, not what it produced.

md_schema.descr: Name of the isothermal whole-genome amplification kit used for this process; record exactly as used in the protocol, for example a commercial multiple displacement or related SAG amplification kit.
Composition or name of the enzyme mix used for isothermal amplification, including any polymerase or accessory enzymes critical to the reaction; record at the start of the process.
Total reaction volume in microliters for the amplification setup; record when the reaction is assembled. Typical values may range from 1 to 100 microliters.

Incubation temperature in degrees Celsius used during the isothermal amplification reaction; record the maintained reaction temperature. Typical values depend on kit chemistry and are often in the 25 to 42 Celsius range.
Total duration in hours of the isothermal amplification reaction; record from reaction start to stop. Typical values may range from 0.5 to 24 hours.
Number of amplification cycles or repeated reaction rounds performed, if applicable to the specific kit or workflow; record at completion of the process.

Total amplified DNA yield in nanograms measured after amplification and before sequencing or library handoff; use as a process output quality indicator for the amplification step. Typical yields may vary widely in SAG workflows.
Qualitative process outcome indicating whether the amplification met minimum acceptance criteria for downstream sequencing; record immediately after completion.

amplified_dna_library.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the amplified DNA library as a material handed off to sequencing: library identifier, source linkage, quantity, concentration, fragment size profile, purity, and storage state. I excluded isothermal amplification protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process, and I excluded sequencing instrument configuration and raw file properties because those belong downstream to Capture and Signal nodes. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I kept the schema focused on the library itself without repeating upstream sample provenance beyond lineage linkage.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the amplified DNA library prepared from the lysate; string format example: 'LIB-0001'. Record once for this sequencing-ready material and use to track it through the workflow.
Identifier of the upstream lysate from which this amplified DNA library was prepared; string format example: 'LYS-0001'. Use to maintain lineage from lysate to sequencing-ready library.

Total amount of amplified DNA available in the library in nanograms at the time of sequencing handoff; measure or estimate before loading the sequencer. Typical values may range from fractions of a nanogram to micrograms depending on amplification success.

DNA concentration of the amplified library in nanograms per microliter at sequencing handoff; measure before instrument loading using the assay used in this workflow. Typical values may range from very low to hundreds of ng per uL.
Typical or modal fragment length of the amplified DNA library in base pairs, measured before sequencing. Record the dominant size estimate used to judge library suitability.
Purity metric for the amplified library, such as A260_over_A280 or a comparable ratio, measured before sequencing handoff to assess contamination or carryover.
Storage temperature in degrees Celsius if the amplified library was held before sequencing; record at storage or transfer. Typical values include 4, -20, or -80 Celsius.
Readiness state of the amplified library at transfer to sequencing; record whether it was ready, required rework, or was rejected before sequencing.

high_throughput_sequencing.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the instrument configuration and session-level acquisition settings used to sequence the amplified DNA library: hardware identity, sequencing platform chemistry, run mode, read layout, loading/input settings, run timing, and a simple run success indicator. I excluded library material properties because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded raw file characteristics because those belong to the downstream Signal. Per the node rules, hardware manufacturer/model/serial belong here, and the sequencing technology itself is captured as an actively configured instrument property rather than as a sample or file attribute.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the high-throughput sequencing instrument used for this capture session; record the hardware vendor name exactly as configured in the run metadata.
Model name or instrument platform used for sequencing; record the specific sequencer model used for the run, for example an instrument in the short-read or long-read category.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session; record the hardware serial exactly as displayed in instrument records for traceability.

Sequencing chemistry or technology actively used in the run, such as short-read or long-read platform chemistry; record at the capture session to describe the configured sequencing approach rather than the sample or file output.
Operational mode of the sequencing run, such as single-end or paired-end acquisition; record at run setup before sequencing begins.

Configured read length in base pairs for the sequencing session; record the planned or instrument-reported read length at run setup. Typical values depend on platform and may range from tens to tens of thousands of base pairs.
Identifier of the flow cell, chip, or cartridge used in the sequencing session; record the consumable ID at instrument loading for traceability.
Amount of amplified DNA library loaded into the sequencer in nanograms; record at sample loading. Typical values are platform-specific and may be low for single amplified genome workflows.
Date and time when the sequencing capture session started; record at instrument run initiation using the instrument clock or laboratory record.
Total duration of the sequencing run in hours from start to completion; record after the run finishes or is terminated.
Outcome of the sequencing run at the capture level; record immediately after completion to indicate whether the run produced usable raw data.

raw_sequence_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact properties: file format, file count, file size, read count, base count, read length distribution, and storage location plus basic technical integrity. I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the upstream Capture, and I excluded assembly or biological interpretation because those belong to downstream Process/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I focused on file-level descriptors needed to find, validate, and reuse the raw reads.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw sequencing reads produced by the sequencer, recorded as the direct digital output format at data export. Examples include FASTQ, BAM, or vendor-native formats.
Number of raw read files associated with this sequencing output; record after run completion when the files are written to storage. Typical values depend on lane or sample splitting.
Total file size of the raw sequencing read output in bytes; record from the storage system after data transfer or export.
Total number of sequencing reads contained in the raw read files; record after primary data generation or from file statistics.
Total number of bases represented in the raw read files; record from file statistics after sequencing output is generated.
Mean read length in base pairs calculated from the raw read files; record from file statistics after sequencing output is generated. Typical values depend on platform and library prep.
Technical integrity flag indicating whether the raw read files are complete and readable without corruption; record after file validation.
Storage location or URI of the raw read files, such as a filesystem path, object-store URI, or accession reference; record after export to the repository or data store.

read_processing_and_assembly.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only computational processing parameters and process-level quality indicators: the software/package used, version, repository or provenance, command or workflow mode, key assembly settings, resource usage, and a summary of assembly success. I excluded raw-read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal, and I excluded contig properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative. Per the node rules, software name, version, and repository are described here because they are agent properties of the operation node.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used for read processing and genome assembly; record the exact tool name used to execute the computational step.
Version of the assembly software used for the computational step; record the release or build version exactly as run, for reproducibility.
Software repository, source, or package reference for the assembly tool; record the URL, package source, or code repository used to obtain the software version executed in the process.
Mode of computational processing applied to the raw reads, such as de novo assembly, read trimming plus assembly, or hybrid assembly; record at workflow execution time.
K-mer size or equivalent key assembly parameter used by the assembly tool, if applicable; record the value set for the run. Typical values depend on assembler and read type.
Minimum contig length threshold in base pairs used during assembly output filtering; record as a process parameter during computational execution.
Number of CPU cores allocated to the assembly computation; record the configured resource setting used for the run.
Amount of RAM in gigabytes allocated to the assembly computation; record the configured resource setting used for the run.
Elapsed run time in hours for the read processing and assembly computation; record from job start to finish.
Outcome of the computational assembly step; record immediately after completion to indicate whether the process finished successfully and produced a usable derivative.

assembled_contigs.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result properties of the contig set: identity/linkage, file representation, count/size/dimension statistics, continuity metrics, and assembly quality indicators. I excluded assembly software and parameter fields because those belong to the upstream Process, and I excluded raw-read file attributes because those belong to the upstream Signal. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I kept the schema focused on the contig output itself and not on biological interpretation beyond assembly-quality summaries.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the assembled contig set produced by the genome assembly step; string format example: 'CONTIGS-0001'. Record once for each assembled derivative.
Identifier of the raw sequencing reads used to generate this contig set; string format example: 'SRR123456'. Use to trace the derivative back to the input signal.
File format used to store the assembled contigs after computation, recorded at output export. Examples include FASTA or FASTQ-like archival formats.
Number of contigs in the assembled output, measured after assembly completion and any output filtering.
Total length in base pairs summed across all contigs in the assembly output; record after assembly completion as a core size statistic.
Length in base pairs of the largest contig in the assembly output; record after assembly completion as a continuity statistic.
N50 contig length in base pairs calculated from the assembled contigs; record after assembly completion as a standard continuity metric.
Overall GC content percentage of the assembled contigs, computed from the final assembly output. Typical values depend on archaeal lineage and environment.
Estimated completeness percentage of the assembled contig set, computed after assembly using the workflow's assessment method. Record as a quality indicator for the derivative.
Estimated contamination percentage of the assembled contig set, computed after assembly using the workflow's assessment method. Record as a quality indicator for the derivative.

genome_reconstruction_analysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational analysis workflow used to derive the final SAG output: software/pipeline identity and provenance, analysis mode, binning/reconstruction criteria, thresholds, and a process-level success indicator. I excluded assembled contig properties because those belong to the upstream Derivative, and I excluded final genome output properties because those belong to the downstream Derivative. Per the node rules, software name, version, and repository are included here because this is the operation node executing the genome reconstruction analysis.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used for genome reconstruction analysis from assembled contigs; record the exact tool or workflow name used to execute this process.
Version of the reconstruction software used for the computational analysis; record the exact release or build version run for reproducibility.
Repository, package source, or code reference for the reconstruction software; record the URL or provenance used to obtain the executed version.
Operational mode of the analysis, such as contig binning, single-genome reconstruction, dereplication, or refinement; record the mode selected for the downstream recovery step.
Minimum contig length in base pairs included in the reconstruction analysis; record the filtering threshold used at analysis time.
Minimum completeness percentage threshold required for an output reconstruction to be accepted; record the acceptance criterion used by the analysis pipeline.
Maximum contamination percentage allowed for an output reconstruction; record the acceptance criterion used by the analysis pipeline.
Number of CPU cores allocated to the genome reconstruction analysis job; record the configured compute resource used.
Amount of RAM in gigabytes allocated to the genome reconstruction analysis; record the configured compute resource used.
Outcome of the genome reconstruction analysis step; record immediately after completion to indicate whether the process produced an acceptable single amplified genome output.

single_amplified_genome_result.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only properties of the computed final SAG result: output identity, lineage linkage, representation, reconstruction size/composition, quality/completeness, and summary statistics that help users interpret the recovered genome. I excluded reconstruction software and thresholds because those belong to the upstream Process, and I excluded raw read or contig file properties because those belong to upstream Signal/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I kept this schema focused on the final genome-derived product without repeating broader sample provenance beyond traceable parent linkage.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final single amplified genome result; string format example: 'SAG-RESULT-0001'. Record once for each reconstructed genome-derived output.
Identifier of the assembled contig set used to generate this final SAG result; string format example: 'CONTIGS-0001'. Use to trace the final derivative back to the assembly output.
File format used to store the final single amplified genome result after reconstruction. Examples include FASTA, GenBank, or annotated genome package formats.
Total length in base pairs of the final reconstructed SAG sequence set; record after genome reconstruction completion as a key size statistic.
Number of contigs retained in the final SAG result; record after reconstruction to indicate the fragmentation level of the recovered genome.
Overall GC content percentage of the final reconstructed SAG; compute from the output sequence set after reconstruction completion.

Estimated completeness percentage of the final single amplified genome result; record after reconstruction using the workflow's assessment method. Typical values may range from low to near complete depending on recovery success.
Estimated contamination percentage of the final single amplified genome result; record after reconstruction using the workflow's assessment method as a quality indicator.
N50 contig length in base pairs for the final SAG output; record as a summary continuity statistic after reconstruction completion.
Whether the final SAG result was annotated or left as a sequence-only reconstruction; record after output generation to indicate downstream interpretability state.
